# Acts of Thomas — Chapter 1
**Agent:** SOPHIA (Consensus)
**Source:** Syriac MS / Greek recension, Acts of Thomas 1

---

## Consensus Translation

*[The apostolic lot. India falls to Thomas. Sold into service.]*

1. At that time all the apostles were gathered in Jerusalem — Simon Peter and Andrew his brother, James the son of Zebedee and John his brother, Philip and Bartholomew, Thomas and Matthew the tax-collector, James the son of Alphaeus and Thaddaeus, Simon the Cananean and Judas Iscariot — and they divided the regions of the world among themselves, so that each would go to the region allotted to him and carry out the word he had received.

2. By lot, India was allotted to Judas Thomas, who is also called Didymus.

3. He was unwilling to go, saying: "I have no strength for this, for I am weak in body. And how can I — a Hebrew — go among the Indians and preach the truth to them?"

4. While he was reasoning and speaking thus, the Lord appeared to him at night in a vision and said: "Fear not, Thomas; go to India and preach the word there, for my grace shall be with you."

5. Still he would not obey, and said: "Send me wherever you will — but not to India."

6. While he continued thus, a certain merchant from India was present in the city — Abbanes by name — who had been dispatched by King Gundaphorus with orders to purchase a skilled carpenter and bring him back.

7. The Lord saw him in the marketplace and said to him: "Do you wish to buy a carpenter?"

8. He said: "Yes."

9. The Lord said: "I have a slave who is a carpenter, and I wish to sell him." And he indicated Thomas to him from a distance.

10. They agreed upon a price of three litrae of uncoined silver, and a bill of sale was written. The writing ran thus: "I, Jesus, son of Joseph the carpenter, residing in Bethlehem of Judaea, hereby declare that I have sold my slave, by name Judas, to you, Abbanes, merchant of Gundaphorus, King of India."

11. When the bill of sale was complete, the Lord took Judas Thomas and brought him to Abbanes the merchant.

12. When Abbanes saw him he said: "Is this man your master?"

13. The apostle answered: "Yes, he is my Lord."

14. Abbanes said to him: "I have purchased you from him." And the apostle was silent.

---

## Textual Notes

- **"Judas Thomas" (v.2):** The Syriac name, meaning "Judas the Twin." The Greek recension often shortens to "Thomas." SOPHIA retains the Syriac full name throughout as the primary source.
- **"Didymus" (v.2):** Greek for "twin" — the Greek translation of the Aramaic *Thomas/Toma*. Retained as a gloss on the name.
- **"Gundaphorus" (v.6):** An Indian king who appears in historical records (Gondophares, 1st century CE). One of the remarkable cases of an apocryphal text preserving genuine historical information.
- **"Three litrae of uncoined silver" (v.10):** A specific monetary detail. The "bill of sale" form is a real legal document genre from the ancient Near East.
- **Thomas's silence (v.14):** Theologically central. The man who argued volubly with the Lord accepts his sale without a word. Surrender to divine will expressed as silence.

---
*SOPHIA synthesis: Chapter 1 establishes the ATH's characteristic blend of comedy, theology, and narrative energy. The bill of sale is rendered in its full legal formality.*
